IVX HOLDINGS — EMERGENCY DEPLOYMENT STABILIZATION
FREEZE FAILED DEPLOYMENTS, RESTORE ONE VERIFIED PRODUCTION RELEASE, PROVIDE APK LATER

OWNER MANDATE — EXECUTE NOW

The Vercel production history shows a large number of failed deployments. This creates a serious risk that reported fixes are not reaching production and that multiple agents are pushing unstable changes.

Do not continue normal production deployment activity.

Do not delete the last successful production deployment.

Do not return a narrative-only report.

==================================================================
1. IMMEDIATE PRODUCTION FREEZE
==================================================================

Immediately:

- Pause all automatic production deployments.
- Pause every AI agent that can push directly to production.
- Pause direct deploys from feature branches.
- Pause database migrations triggered automatically.
- Preserve the currently working production deployment.
- Preserve all logs, failed builds and deployment metadata.
- Keep the public application online using the last successful release.
- Do not roll back unless the current live release is unhealthy.

Development and testing may continue only in:

- Local environments.
- Preview environments.
- Staging.
- Isolated test databases.
- Verified release branches.

==================================================================
2. IDENTIFY THE REAL LIVE VERSION
==================================================================

Return and verify:

- Production platform.
- Production project name.
- Active production domain.
- Last successful deployment ID.
- Last successful deployment timestamp.
- Active production commit SHA.
- GitHub repository.
- Active branch.
- GitHub HEAD SHA.
- Runtime build version.
- Runtime commit SHA.
- Health endpoint.
- Health endpoint HTTP status.
- Boot time.

The following must be compared:

GITHUB HEAD
VERSUS
LAST SUCCESSFUL DEPLOYMENT SHA
VERSUS
ACTIVE PRODUCTION SHA
VERSUS
RUNTIME HEALTH SHA

Do not claim production is current unless these values match.

==================================================================
3. AUDIT ALL FAILED DEPLOYMENTS
==================================================================

Audit failed deployments from newest to oldest.

Create a failure table containing:

- Deployment ID.
- Commit SHA.
- Branch.
- Commit message.
- Triggering agent or user.
- Start time.
- End time.
- Build duration.
- Failure stage.
- Exact error.
- File.
- Function.
- Line number.
- Missing variable, if applicable.
- Migration involved.
- Whether production data was touched.
- Root cause category.
- Duplicate of another failure: yes or no.
- Corrective action.
- Status.

Group the failures into root-cause categories:

- TypeScript or compile failure.
- Dependency failure.
- Missing environment variable.
- Invalid secret binding.
- Authentication failure.
- Database migration failure.
- Schema mismatch.
- SQL error.
- API route error.
- Build configuration error.
- Platform configuration error.
- Conflicting agent changes.
- Unsupported runtime.
- Timeout.
- Memory failure.
- Invalid branch or repository binding.

Do not fix hundreds of deployments individually when they share the same root cause.

==================================================================
4. VERIFY THE PRODUCTION PLATFORM
==================================================================

Confirm whether the web production application is intended to run on:

- Vercel,
- Render,
- or another service.

Do not maintain two conflicting production control planes.

Return:

- Which service hosts the web frontend.
- Which service hosts the backend API.
- Which service is authoritative for production.
- Which deployments are obsolete.
- Which repositories and branches trigger each service.
- Whether Vercel is still required.
- Whether Render is still required.
- Recommended final architecture.

Do not remove a service until its production responsibility is verified and safely migrated.

==================================================================
5. STOP DIRECT AGENT DEPLOYMENTS
==================================================================

No AI agent may push directly to production.

Required release workflow:

AGENT DEVELOPMENT
→ FEATURE BRANCH
→ AUTOMATED TESTS
→ CODE REVIEW
→ SECURITY REVIEW
→ STAGING DEPLOYMENT
→ STAGING QA
→ RELEASE CANDIDATE
→ OWNER APPROVAL WHEN REQUIRED
→ SINGLE PRODUCTION DEPLOYMENT
→ LIVE VERIFICATION
→ COMPLETE

Create one release manager:

IVX RELEASE MANAGER AI

Only this agent may prepare a production release after all required checks pass.

IVX IA Senior Developer may write and test code but must not bypass the release gate.

==================================================================
6. CREATE ONE CLEAN RELEASE BRANCH
==================================================================

Create one release branch from the last known-good production commit.

Example:

release/ivx-production-stable

Then:

- Cherry-pick only verified fixes.
- Remove duplicated or conflicting commits.
- Resolve merge conflicts.
- Validate package-lock or equivalent lockfile.
- Validate build configuration.
- Validate all environment-variable references.
- Validate database migrations.
- Run a clean install.
- Run a clean production build.
- Run automated tests.
- Deploy to staging.
- Run staging acceptance tests.
- Create a release candidate.
- Deploy once to production.

Do not use the current production branch as an uncontrolled testing branch.

==================================================================
7. DATABASE SAFETY
==================================================================

Before any new deployment:

- Back up the production database.
- Record the current schema version.
- Record migration history.
- Detect partially applied migrations.
- Detect code/schema mismatch.
- Validate Row Level Security.
- Validate indexes.
- Validate required functions and triggers.
- Validate rollback scripts.
- Use transaction-safe migrations where possible.

Do not rerun migrations blindly.

Do not delete or rewrite production records without owner approval and a verified backup.

==================================================================
8. REQUIRED PRE-DEPLOYMENT GATES
==================================================================

A release cannot deploy unless all required checks pass:

- Clean dependency installation.
- TypeScript compilation.
- Linting.
- Unit tests.
- Integration tests.
- API tests.
- Authentication tests.
- Authorization tests.
- Database migration dry run.
- Production build.
- Staging deployment.
- Staging health check.
- Owner login.
- Members loading.
- Investors loading.
- Buyers loading.
- Deals loading.
- Reels loading.
- Chat send and receive.
- Landing page.
- Security review.
- Rollback readiness.

Any failed mandatory gate blocks production deployment.

==================================================================
9. FINAL PRODUCTION DEPLOYMENT
==================================================================

After all gates pass:

1. Record the last stable deployment.
2. Create the rollback tag.
3. Create the release tag.
4. Deploy the backend.
5. Verify backend health.
6. Deploy the frontend.
7. Verify public production routes.
8. Verify owner authentication.
9. Verify production data.
10. Verify logs.
11. Compare all commit SHAs.
12. Monitor errors after deployment.
13. Keep rollback available.
14. Mark production verified only after live tests pass.

==================================================================
10. APK MAY BE PROVIDED AFTER WEB STABILIZATION
==================================================================

The Android APK does not need to block emergency web-production stabilization.

Rork may provide the APK later, but it must be tracked as a separate required release task.

Create:

TASK: IVX-ANDROID-APK-FINAL

Status initially:

PENDING AFTER WEB STABILIZATION

APK requirements:

- Built from the same verified release commit.
- Production configuration.
- Correct API URL.
- Correct Supabase project.
- No development banners.
- No Rork branding.
- Owner login verified.
- Members verified.
- Investors verified.
- Buyers verified.
- Deals verified.
- Reels verified.
- Chat verified.
- Session persistence verified.
- Physical Android installation tested.
- Version and build number displayed.
- Direct installation link provided.

Required APK evidence:

- APK filename.
- APK version.
- Build number.
- EAS build ID or build-system ID.
- Source commit SHA.
- Build timestamp.
- File size.
- Checksum.
- Direct download link.
- Installation result.
- Physical-device test result.

The APK must not be marked complete merely because a build command started.

==================================================================
11. AAB AND IOS TRACKING
==================================================================

Create separate release tasks:

- IVX-ANDROID-AAB-FINAL
- IVX-IOS-BUILD-FINAL

These may remain pending while the web application is stabilized, but they must not be reported as complete.

For every blocked build, return:

- Missing service or account.
- Expected credential name.
- Runtime binding result.
- Exact error.
- Corrective action.
- Owner action required, if genuinely necessary.
- Target completion after access is restored.

==================================================================
12. LIVE DEPLOYMENT DASHBOARD
==================================================================

Add a deployment-control section showing:

- Production freeze status.
- Current live deployment.
- Current live SHA.
- Last successful deployment.
- Failed-deployment count.
- Root-cause groups.
- Release candidate.
- Staging status.
- Required gates.
- Passed gates.
- Failed gates.
- Active deployment.
- Rollback version.
- APK status.
- AAB status.
- iOS status.
- Responsible agent.
- Last heartbeat.
- Next action.
- Exact blocker.

==================================================================
13. FIRST RESPONSE REQUIRED
==================================================================

Return this table with real evidence:

| Item | Required result |
| Production freeze | Enabled or exact failure |
| Live site | Online or offline |
| Current live deployment | Deployment ID |
| Current live commit | Full SHA |
| GitHub HEAD | Full SHA |
| SHA match | PASS or FAIL |
| Health endpoint | URL, HTTP status and timestamp |
| Failed deployments | Exact count |
| Root-cause groups | Count and categories |
| Direct agent deploys | Disabled or exact failure |
| Release manager | Agent ID and status |
| Stable release branch | Branch name |
| Staging | URL and status |
| Database backup | Backup ID and timestamp |
| Migration status | Clean, partial or failed |
| Rollback | Deployment ID and tag |
| APK task | Task ID and current status |
| APK target | Date and time |
| AAB task | Status |
| iOS task | Status |
| Current blocker | Exact technical evidence |
| Next update | Exact time |

==================================================================
14. FINAL ACCEPTANCE
==================================================================

The emergency deployment issue is resolved only when:

- Failed automatic deployments are stopped.
- One authoritative production platform is confirmed.
- The actual live commit is known.
- GitHub, deployment and runtime SHAs match.
- Failed deployments are grouped by real root cause.
- One clean release branch exists.
- All required release gates pass.
- One verified production deployment succeeds.
- Rollback is tested and available.
- IVX IA agents cannot bypass the release gate.
- APK remains tracked and is delivered afterward from the same verified source commit.

Allowed final status:

PRODUCTION PIPELINE STABILIZED — VERIFIED

or

BLOCKED — EXACT TECHNICAL EVIDENCE

Do not return “production complete” while automated deployments continue failing.
